observations.seen: In frame 1 the floor in front of the treasure chest is blown out to near-white while the walls stay murky grey-brown. The ceiling strip lights cast soft pools but give no clear light direction. Frame 4 is lit by a uniform orange wash that flattens every surface.

There are almost no visible cast shadows. The chest in frame 1 and the pillar in frame 2 have no grounding contact shadow. Wall bases get only a faint dark gradient. The floating pistol in frames 3 and 4 casts nothing.

The floors show a single smeared specular streak under each light (frames 2 and 3) but no environment detail. The flooded-cellar water in frames 2 and 3 is a flat opaque teal plane with no reflection or refraction.

The corridors are long boxes with repeated pipe runs and yellow kick strips. The round vault door at the end of frames 3 and 4 is the only landmark. There is no Cold-War set dressing such as signage clutter, crates, consoles or cabling, so the spaces read as greybox with textures applied.

A teal distance fog in frames 2 and 3 adds some depth. The four-point sparkle sprites in frame 2 float in the air like UI glyphs. The pickup glow is a hard-edged white ellipse rather than a volumetric bloom.

The stone wall texture in frames 2 and 3 is stretched and uniformly tiled with no normal or parallax depth at the edges. The concrete walls in frames 1 and 4 are flat albedo with faint smudges. The chest in frame 1 is washed out and looks semi-transparent. The water reads as plastic.

Wall geometry is plain extruded blocks with cylinder pipes and sharp untrimmed corners. The pistol has decent detail but is shown with no hands or arms, and it floats beside the view pointing right and away from the crosshair.

Frames 3 and 4 are centered one-point-perspective corridor shots with large empty floor areas filling the lower half. The pistol sits mid-right and blocks the sightline. Frame 1's focal chest is lost in the overexposed floor.
The viewmodel placement in frames 3 and 4 is unnatural: the gun is mid-screen, rotated outward, and detached. FOV and eye height are reasonable, but the weapon framing breaks first-person presence.

Tone mapping clips highlights on the frame 1 floor and the frame 2 pickup. Bloom is heavy on the floor lights in frame 4. A dark vignette and color grade are visible, but there is no AA cleanup on the pipe silhouettes and no depth of field or grain cohesion.

The bottom stat bar with health, armor, ammo, score, kills and time is clean and legible. However, the pickup and kill log stacks six identical-style toasts, and a browser-style mode and floor tab bar sits on top of the game view. Frames 3 and 4 show no HUD at all.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
